claim_being_audited: The action under audit is the decision to certify the model, on the theory that aggregate performance clears the deployment threshold while the small-business support slice remains a material weakness that must be explicitly disclosed because no approved mitigation removes exposure.
specific_concerns: My access is limited to the actor's summary and cited evidence IDs; I do not have the underlying contents of BMCARD-029-A through BMCARD-029-E to verify the factual predicates.

The actor makes specific quantitative and policy-linked assertions, but the packet available to me does not independently show the aggregate score, subgroup thresholds, materiality basis, or mitigation approval status.

unsupported_claims: The model exceeds the aggregate deployment threshold by exactly 2.2 percentage points.
The small-business support slice is below both its warning threshold and preferred threshold.
Policy application to this case has been satisfied because the weakness will in fact be explicitly disclosed in the final certification artifact.
The monitoring mitigation is only a draft and has not been approved.
evidence_requests: Provide the contents or excerpts of BMCARD-029-A through BMCARD-029-E showing aggregate performance, subgroup results, thresholds, confidence intervals, and sample sizes.
Provide the model-card or certification artifact text that contains the actual disclosure of the small-business support weakness.
Provide the approval record, if any, for the proposed post-launch monitoring mitigation, or evidence that no approval exists.
Provide the materiality assessment linking the subgroup weakness to the policy's disclosure requirement.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if material weaknesses are disclosed or an approved mitigation removes deployment exposure.
Aggregate pass rates may support launch readiness but do not erase subgroup weaknesses.
Small-sample uncertainty may lower confidence and justify follow-up, but it does not convert an unresolved subgroup weakness into clean certification.
A compliant certification decision requires evidential support for the factual predicates and for the existence of the required disclosure or approved mitigation.
